A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HiCI with the same authors and core architecture. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original HiCI language-modeling, retrieval, LongBench, ablation, training-efficiency, and attention-analysis results.

after.justification: v3 retains original HiCI experiments and adds Qwen3-8B results, additional comparator results, and a global-context causality ablation.

M1.justification: The main construction–integration–broadcast algorithm and Equations 1–13 remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 introduces a tested variant, Gi = Agg(L1, ..., Li), that restricts global aggregation to current and preceding segments instead of the entire sequence. This is a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Both versions use RedPajama and LongAlpaca-12k for training and PG-19, Proof-pile, passkey retrieval, LongChat topic retrieval, and LongBench for evaluation. Qwen3 adds a model configuration within existing tasks and context-length coverage, rather than a new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds unadapted LLaMA-2 and ChunkLLaMA comparisons, plus a base-Qwen3 comparison. Topic-retrieval Table 2 replaces GPT-3.5-Turbo-16K and Claude-1.3-100K with GPT-4o-mini-128K and Claude-3.5-Sonnet-200K, and adds Llama-3-8B-Instruct-8K. These substantially expand and revise the reported comparator set. GPT-3.5 remains in the unchanged LongBench comparison.

E3.justification: v3 adds Qwen3-8B adaptation from 32K to 48K with 500- and 1,000-step configurations, plus a controlled global-context experiment. It also changes the stated evaluation mode for retained component/cardinality ablations from hierarchical attention to standard full attention despite unchanged scores. This establishes a reported protocol revision, not evidence of rerunning. Table 1's mode remains ambiguous: Section 4.1 specifies hierarchical attention, whereas Table 6 describes full attention as consistent with Table 1.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a control testing whether access to future segments explains HiCI's gains; Appendix B.2 adds a component-wise FLOPs comparison. Conversely, v1's Table 5 comparing segment sizes, attention modes, and evaluation-length sensitivity is removed. The existing segment-size training-loss curves and layer-wise attention analyses remain, so this is a substantive change in analytical evidence rather than wholesale removal of segment-size analysis.

E5.justification: Removing v1 Table 5 also removes its standard-deviation summaries across evaluation lengths. This is a limited removal of descriptive dispersion reporting, not evidence of fewer training seeds or repeated runs. Both versions retain ten randomized passkey trials per context length; neither reports training-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial result entries while retaining the existing LLaMA-2 language-modeling, LongBench, and component-ablation numbers. New Qwen3 results at 48K include PG-19 perplexity 9.73 and Proof-pile 2.26, alongside base-model values 11.32 and 2.46. Table 6 adds restricted-aggregation perplexities 7.28/7.00/6.94 versus shared-context 7.27/7.01/6.93. New comparator and FLOPs results are reported, while v1 Table 5's segment-granularity results disappear.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly formalizes Gi = Agg(L1, ..., Li) and identifies the original global aggregation's non-causal cross-segment pathway. The information-capacity bound, data-processing inequality, computational-complexity theorem, and their existing derivations remain unchanged. No new causality proof is supplied.

C1.justification: Cross-family applicability changes from a proposed future direction to a claimed demonstrated contribution through Qwen3-8B. The introduction and conclusion remove near length-invariant perplexity as a headline finding, and the advertised parameter overhead changes from approximately 5.5% to 4–5%. The conclusion additionally claims superiority to ChunkLLaMA across all evaluated lengths, although Table 1 contains counterexamples.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 newly acknowledges future-segment access and interprets the control results as evidence that hierarchical structure, rather than that access, drives gains. The new Limitations section explicitly identifies growing decoding KV-cache costs and untested benefits for models with native contexts of 128K or longer. The earlier interpretation linking attention stability to near length-invariant perplexity is removed.

D1.justification: Table 9 gains a Qwen3-8B pretraining configuration, documenting optimizer, LoRA, batch, slot, and bottleneck settings. Section 4.1 specifies 8×H200 GPUs for Qwen3 while retaining 8×H100 for LLaMA-2. Existing LLaMA-2 hyperparameters and the paper's code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 2.4 substantially expands positioning relative to global-workspace architectures and latent representations, including VanRullen and Kanai, Goyal et al., Zeng et al., concept-centric transformers, Coconut, and Large Concept Models. It distinguishes HiCI's within-layer context aggregation from inter-module coordination and latent reasoning or prediction. Additional references support the new model and baseline comparisons.

P1.justification: v3 revises the abstract, contribution bullets, experimental discussion, and conclusion; separates language modeling and retrieval into distinct subsections; and adds dedicated related-work and limitations sections. The method exposition and most existing appendix prose remain substantially intact, making this a localized narrative revision rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands its model/comparator blocks, Table 9 gains a Qwen3 column, and Table 2 changes comparator rows. New Tables 6 and 10 display the causality and FLOPs analyses, while v1 Table 5 is removed. All five figures retain their designs and plotted content, with relocation and associated page reflow. The placeholder running header is corrected.

improvement.justification: The new model comparisons, related-work distinctions, causality discussion, and limitations improve breadth and transparency. However, Section 4.1 and Table 6 conflict over the attention mode underlying central perplexity results, while unchanged ablation scores receive a different protocol description. The new causal control leaves handling of within-segment future information unspecified, and the earlier segment-perplexity evidence is removed. These uncertainties affect the central validation, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
